newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel interventions not inflationary.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel interventions not inflationary.

text.p: Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel said the central bank's recent interventions in the foreign currency markets were not inflationary as other monetary measures were being taken.
"All injections are being sterilised. There is no single shekel in the market beyond what we want," Frenkel told Reuters on Tuesday.
The central bank has been buying foreign currency frequently in the past month to prevent the shekel from strengthening beyond its permitted trading band.
Israeli banks estimate the central bank has injected more than a billion shekels through its interventions.

"Daily (monetary) auctions and other monetary instruments are being used to ensure that the interventions are not allowed to alter the base of monetary expansion beyond what we in the bank think is warranted," Frenkel said.
On September 2 the central bank suspended its daily auctions for loans to commercial banks in light of excess liquidity. The auctions were resumed on September 17.
Frenkel blamed pressures in the foreign exchange market on the government's widening budget deficit and not on interest rates.
